question: Who built the famous stupa of Bharhut originally?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maurya **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maurya:**

 
 
• The Bharhut stupa was originally built during the Maurya dynasty, specifically during the reign of Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• Ashoka was a great patron of Buddhism and built numerous stupas across his empire.
 
• The original Maurya structure was likely a simpler brick stupa.
 
• Later, the Sunga dynasty significantly enhanced and expanded the stupa.
 
• The site is very important for the study of early Indian art.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sunga:**

 
 
• The Sunga dynasty, which succeeded the Mauryas, significantly enlarged and embellished the Bharhut stupa in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• They added the elaborate stone railings and gateways with intricate carvings.
 
• The Sunga period is known for its distinctive style of sculptural art, which is evident at Bharhut.
 
• The Sunga's added many of the famous carvings that are now associated with the Bharhut stupa.
 
• They greatly contributed to the current look of the stupa.
 
 
 
• **Satavahana:**
 
 
• The Satavahana dynasty ruled in the Deccan region of India.
 
• They were known for their patronage of Buddhism and their contributions to art and architecture, particularly at sites like Amaravati and Sanchi.
 
• They were not primarily associated with the Bharhut stupa.
 
• They were a very powerful dynasty in southern India.
 
• They were known for their trade.
 
 
 
• **Kushan:**
 
 
• The Kushan Empire, which flourished in northern India and Central Asia, was known for its Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.
 
• They were also patrons of Buddhism and built numerous stupas and monasteries.
 
• However, they were not the original builders of the Bharhut stupa.
 
• They were famous for the Gandhara style of art.
 
• They played a large role in the spread of Buddhism.
